
```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(ranger)
library(glmnet)
library(themis)

employee <- read_csv("week13_employee.csv")

glimpse(employee)
dim(employee)
head(employee)
```

```{r data_preparation}
# Check missing values
colSums(is.na(employee))

# Check employee attrition
table(employee$Attrition)

# Calculate attrition percentages
prop.table(table(employee$Attrition)) * 100

# Convert outcome to factor
employee <- employee %>%
  mutate(
    Attrition = factor(
      Attrition,
      levels = c("Yes", "No")
    ),
    across(where(is.character), as.factor)
  )

# Confirm factor levels
levels(employee$Attrition)

# Check structure
glimpse(employee)
```

```{r attrition_graph}
ggplot(employee, aes(x = Attrition, fill = Attrition)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Employee Attrition Distribution",
    x = "Employee Attrition",
    y = "Number of Employees"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r job_satisfaction_graph}
employee %>%
  group_by(SatisfactionJob) %>%
  summarise(
    AttritionRate = mean(Attrition == "Yes") * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = factor(SatisfactionJob),
    y = AttritionRate
  )) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Attrition Rate by Job Satisfaction",
    x = "Job Satisfaction Level",
    y = "Attrition Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r data_splitting}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Split data: 80% training and 20% testing
employee_split <- initial_split(
  employee,
  prop = 0.80,
  strata = Attrition
)

# Create training and testing datasets
train_data <- training(employee_split)
test_data <- testing(employee_split)

# Check dimensions
dim(train_data)
dim(test_data)

# Check attrition distribution
table(train_data$Attrition)
table(test_data$Attrition)
```

```{r preprocessing}
# Create preprocessing recipe
employee_recipe <- recipe(
  Attrition ~ .,
  data = train_data
) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

# Display recipe
employee_recipe
```

```{r logistic_regression}
# Define logistic regression model
log_model <- logistic_reg() %>%
  set_engine("glm") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

# Create modelling workflow
log_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(employee_recipe) %>%
  add_model(log_model)

# Train the model
log_fit <- fit(
  log_workflow,
  data = train_data
)

# Display model
log_fit
```

```{r cross_validation}
set.seed(123)

# Create 5-fold cross-validation
employee_folds <- vfold_cv(
  train_data,
  v = 5,
  strata = Attrition
)

employee_folds
```

```{r logistic_evaluation}
# Evaluate logistic regression
log_cv <- fit_resamples(
  log_workflow,
  resamples = employee_folds,
  metrics = metric_set(
    precision,
    recall,
    accuracy,
    roc_auc
  ),
  control = control_resamples(
    save_pred = TRUE
  )
)

# Display evaluation results
collect_metrics(log_cv)
```

```{r random_forest_model}
# Define Random Forest model
rf_model <- rand_forest(
  trees = 500,
  mtry = 5,
  min_n = 10
) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

# Create Random Forest workflow
rf_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(employee_recipe) %>%
  add_model(rf_model)

# Display workflow
rf_workflow
```

```{r random_forest_evaluation}
set.seed(123)

# Evaluate Random Forest using same folds
rf_cv <- fit_resamples(
  rf_workflow,
  resamples = employee_folds,
  metrics = metric_set(
    precision,
    recall,
    accuracy,
    roc_auc
  ),
  control = control_resamples(
    save_pred = TRUE
  )
)

# Display results
collect_metrics(rf_cv)
```

```{r threshold_analysis}
# Collect cross-validation predictions
rf_predictions <- collect_predictions(rf_cv)

# Compare classification thresholds
threshold_results <- map_dfr(
  c(0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60, 0.70),
  function(threshold) {

    predictions <- rf_predictions %>%
      mutate(
        predicted_class = factor(
          if_else(
            .pred_Yes >= threshold,
            "Yes",
            "No"
          ),
          levels = c("Yes", "No")
        )
      )

    tibble(
      Threshold = threshold,
      Precision = precision(
        predictions,
        truth = Attrition,
        estimate = predicted_class
      )$.estimate,
      Recall = recall(
        predictions,
        truth = Attrition,
        estimate = predicted_class
      )$.estimate,
      Predicted_Yes = sum(
        predictions$predicted_class == "Yes"
      )
    )
  }
)

print(threshold_results)
```

```{r pca_preprocessing}
# Create PCA preprocessing recipe
pca_recipe <- recipe(
  Attrition ~ .,
  data = train_data
) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_pca(all_numeric_predictors(),
           threshold = 0.95)

# Display PCA recipe
pca_recipe
```

```{r pca_model}
# Create logistic regression workflow with PCA
pca_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(pca_recipe) %>%
  add_model(log_model)

# Evaluate using same cross-validation folds
set.seed(123)

pca_cv <- fit_resamples(
  pca_workflow,
  resamples = employee_folds,
  metrics = metric_set(
    precision,
    recall,
    accuracy,
    roc_auc
  ),
  control = control_resamples(
    save_pred = TRUE
  )
)

# Display PCA model performance
collect_metrics(pca_cv)
```

```{r model_comparison}
# Combine cross-validation results
comparison <- bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(log_cv) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Logistic Regression"),
  collect_metrics(rf_cv) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Random Forest"),
  collect_metrics(pca_cv) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Logistic Regression + PCA")
) %>%
  select(Model, .metric, mean) %>%
  mutate(mean = round(mean * 100, 2))

print(comparison)
```

```{r final_model_evaluation}
# Train Random Forest on the full training dataset
set.seed(123)

final_rf_fit <- fit(
  rf_workflow,
  data = train_data
)

# Predict probabilities on the test dataset
test_predictions <- bind_cols(
  test_data %>% select(Attrition),
  predict(
    final_rf_fit,
    new_data = test_data,
    type = "prob"
  )
)

# Apply the selected 0.60 threshold
test_predictions <- test_predictions %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_class = factor(
      if_else(
        .pred_Yes >= 0.60,
        "Yes",
        "No"
      ),
      levels = c("Yes", "No")
    )
  )

# Display confusion matrix
conf_mat(
  test_predictions,
  truth = Attrition,
  estimate = predicted_class
)

# Calculate final performance metrics
final_metrics <- metric_set(
  precision,
  recall,
  accuracy,
  roc_auc
)(
  test_predictions,
  truth = Attrition,
  estimate = predicted_class,
  .pred_Yes
)

print(final_metrics)
```

```{r overfitting_check}
# Predict probabilities on training data
train_predictions <- bind_cols(
  train_data %>% select(Attrition),
  predict(final_rf_fit, train_data, type = "prob")
) %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_class = factor(
      if_else(.pred_Yes >= 0.60, "Yes", "No"),
      levels = c("Yes", "No")
    )
  )

# Calculate training metrics
train_metrics <- metric_set(
  precision, recall, accuracy, roc_auc
)(
  train_predictions,
  truth = Attrition,
  estimate = predicted_class,
  .pred_Yes
)

# Compare training and testing results
performance_comparison <- bind_rows(
  train_metrics %>%
    mutate(Dataset = "Training"),
  final_metrics %>%
    mutate(Dataset = "Testing")
) %>%
  select(Dataset, .metric, .estimate) %>%
  mutate(
    .estimate = round(.estimate * 100, 2)
  )

print(performance_comparison)
```
## Conclusion and Management Recommendations

This analysis investigated factors associated with employee attrition and developed classification models to predict whether employees are likely to leave the organisation.

The exploratory analysis identified several factors associated with attrition, including job satisfaction, employee age, business travel frequency, years at the company, and work-life balance satisfaction. Employees with lower job satisfaction, shorter tenure, and frequent business travel generally demonstrated higher attrition rates.

Three classification approaches were compared: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression with PCA. Random Forest achieved the highest cross-validation precision of 73.2% at the standard classification threshold.

To meet management's preference for high precision, a classification threshold of 0.60 was selected. On the testing dataset, Random Forest achieved 100% precision, 4.17% recall, 84.4% accuracy, and 80.8% ROC-AUC.

However, the model correctly identified only 2 of the 48 employees who left. The substantial difference between training and testing ROC-AUC also suggests overfitting.

Overall, Random Forest was the strongest candidate for management's high-precision objective among the models tested. Nevertheless, its low recall and limited number of positive predictions mean that it should not be relied upon as a standalone decision-making tool.

Management should consider further model tuning, additional relevant employee data, and validation on new datasets before operational use. Any retention interventions should be supportive, confidential, and based on employee feedback rather than predictions alone.
